identification.summary: North Korean state-sponsored actor that pursues espionage, data theft, financial gain and network destruction, typically targeting media, IT services and defense organizations worldwide [S1][S2]. Microsoft tracks it as one of several separate North Korean clusters that public reporting often groups as 'Lazarus Group'.
identification.firstObserved: US charges tie the Lazarus-associated program to the 2014 Sony Pictures attack and 2016–2017 operations [S3]. Microsoft reporting on Diamond Sleet specifically covers 2022–2023 activity [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Diamond Sleet (formerly ZINC). Microsoft maps ZINC, LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA, Black Artemis and Lazarus to it [S6]; Microsoft also notes overlap with Temp.Hermit [S1]. The imported record merged the whole Lazarus umbrella. Names Microsoft and MITRE track separately have been moved out of the alias list (see Related Microsoft clusters): Andariel/APT45/Silent Chollima (Onyx Sleet), BlueNoroff/APT38/Stardust Chollima (Sapphire Sleet and MITRE G0082), TraderTraitor/UNC4899 (Jade Sleet), AppleJeus/UNC4736 (Citrine Sleet), Storm-1789 (Moonstone Sleet).

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea: Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB)-associated hacking program, per US charging documents describing the Lazarus Group [S3].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the 2023 CyberLink supply-chain compromise to Diamond Sleet with HIGH confidence [S1]. US government attribution of the broader Lazarus program through the 2018 criminal complaint and Treasury sanctions on Chosun Expo [S3].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and malware analysis [S1][S2]; DOJ complaint and Treasury designations [S3]; long-running US-CERT HIDDEN COBRA reporting [S7].

objectives: Espionage, data theft, financial gain and network destruction in support of DPRK regime priorities, including revenue generation that evades sanctions [S1][S2][S3].

regions: Global, including Japan, Taiwan, Canada and the United States (CyberLink victims)
targeting.notes: Sectors from Microsoft [S1][S2]. Financial and crypto targeting is a feature of the wider Lazarus-associated program [S3]. The $1.5B Bybit theft (Feb 2025) was attributed by the FBI to TraderTraitor, which Microsoft tracks as Jade Sleet rather than Diamond Sleet [S4].

capabilities.summary: Software supply-chain compromise: a modified CyberLink installer signed with a valid CyberLink certificate and hosted on CyberLink's update infrastructure delivered LambLoad to over 100 devices [S1]. Rapid n-day exploitation of JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2023-42793 from early October 2023, using the ForestTiger backdoor (LSASS credential dumping) and RollSling (DLL search-order hijacking) [S2]. Destructive capability demonstrated in the 2014 Sony attack attributed to the Lazarus program [S3]. MITRE lists 93 techniques for Lazarus Group (G0032) [S5].

campaigns.name: Sony Pictures Entertainment attack
campaigns.summary: Destructive attack and data leak attributed to the Lazarus-associated program in the 2018 DOJ complaint.

campaigns.name: Bangladesh Bank SWIFT theft
campaigns.summary: $81 million stolen. Named in the 2018 complaint; MITRE separates this financial activity under APT38 (G0082).

campaigns.name: WannaCry
campaigns.summary: Global ransomware worm attributed to the Lazarus-associated program in the 2018 complaint.

campaigns.name: DOJ complaint against Park Jin Hyok
campaigns.summary: First US criminal charges against a North Korean hacker; Treasury sanctions Park and Chosun Expo Joint Venture.

campaigns.name: TeamCity CVE-2023-42793 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Diamond Sleet and Onyx Sleet exploit JetBrains TeamCity servers; Diamond Sleet deploys ForestTiger and RollSling.

campaigns.name: CyberLink supply-chain compromise
campaigns.summary: Modified, validly signed CyberLink installer (LambLoad) reaches over 100 devices in Japan, Taiwan, Canada, the US and elsewhere. High-confidence Microsoft attribution.

diamond.adversary: DPRK RGB-associated operators; Park Jin Hyok named in the 2018 complaint as part of the Lazarus-associated program [S3].
diamond.capability: Supply-chain trojanization with stolen or abused code-signing; n-day exploitation; ForestTiger, RollSling, LambLoad; destructive malware [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Legitimate vendor update infrastructure abused for distribution; compromised and actor-controlled C2 servers [S1].
diamond.victim: Media, defense and IT organizations worldwide; software-vendor customers [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Regime intelligence needs and sanctions-evading revenue; retaliation against perceived insults, as with Sony [S3].
diamond.technology: Trust in signed software and update channels; slow patching of developer infrastructure such as CI/CD servers [S1][S2].

gaps: Diamond Sleet-specific reporting after 2023 was not gathered in this pass.
Boundary between Diamond Sleet and the other Sleet clusters in historical 'Lazarus' reporting. Older events (Sony, WannaCry) are attributed to the Lazarus program, not to Diamond Sleet specifically.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The OE includes software vendors and CI/CD infrastructure that supply DoD and DIB networks; supply-chain paths are key terrain. STEP 2: A validly signed installer defeats allow-listing based on signer trust, so terrain analysis must include update channels. STEP 3: The template is n-day exploitation of developer infrastructure or trojanized signed software, then credential theft (ForestTiger) and hijack-based persistence (RollSling), then espionage or destruction. STEP 4: MLCOA is espionage against defense and IT targets with opportunistic financial theft. MDCOA is a destructive attack, Sony-style, against a high-profile target during a Korean Peninsula crisis. Candidate indicators: unexpected child processes from vendor updaters, DLL search-order hijacks in IT tools, and newly exploited CI/CD CVEs [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Supply-chain visibility: JCC2 data should flag vendor-signed binaries behaving abnormally, not just unsigned code. (2) Coordinate with INDOPACOM and USFK on Korean Peninsula crisis I&W, since DPRK cyber activity can precede or accompany provocations. (3) Revenue-focused operations (crypto theft) are a Treasury, FBI and law-enforcement lead, but they finance regime programs and so are relevant to campaign-level assessment. (4) Naming discipline: reporting chains should carry the specific cluster (Diamond, Onyx, Jade, Sapphire Sleet), because 'Lazarus' aggregates distinct actors with different targets.
